title: Robot Data Startup Mecka AI Raises $60M Led by Sequoia Capital
key_facts: Mecka AI raised $60 million in a Series B round led by Sequoia Capital; Nvidia and Microsoft's M12 also took part.
Founded in 2024, it pays people to record themselves doing everyday tasks with body sensors and smartphones.
The data trains humanoid and other robots; Mecka uses an 'egocentric' first-person approach, different from teleoperation.
Mecka reportedly approached a $500 million valuation before this round.
Rival XDOF reportedly nears a $1.2 billion valuation; Scale AI and Micro1 are also moving into robotics data.
Mecka projects a $100 million annual revenue run rate by end of 2026, per CEO Josh Gao's comments to Fortune.
None of the four co-founders comes from a robotics background.
